post_copy: Most Shopify SEO advice still focuses on Google. I am testing a small scanner that checks whether product pages have fields AI engines can understand, like material, barcode, brand, reviews, and availability. Curious if other merchants are seeing ChatGPT/Perplexity traffic yet.

I scanned a batch of Shopify products and the most common AI visibility gaps were missing barcode, material, and review signals. Product descriptions alone are not enough if the structured fields are thin.
I built a free AI readiness scanner for Shopify products. It checks up to 20 products and shows which product fields may make the catalog harder for ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Gemini to understand.
One practical GEO fix: make product descriptions include material, use case, dimensions, variant context, and brand. AI engines need concrete product facts, not only marketing copy.
If a store has 100+ products, manually checking product data quality is slow. A scan-first workflow helps find the products where missing fields have the biggest score impact.
Question for Shopify owners: are you optimizing product pages for AI search yet, or still only Google SEO? I am collecting feedback on what merchants actually care about here.
Week one learning from AI product visibility scans: missing structured product details are more common than bad titles. Barcode, material, size, color, and review data matter.
Quick checklist for Shopify AI visibility: brand, description, image, availability, SKU, barcode, material, color, size, MPN, reviews, price, and product URL.
GEO is not magic. It is mostly making product data complete enough for AI systems to understand what each product is, who it is for, and when to recommend it.
I am looking for Shopify merchants with 50+ products to test a free product AI readiness scan. It gives a score and missing field breakdown; no signup for the first scan.
For dropshipping and POD stores, repeated supplier descriptions make products harder to differentiate. Adding concrete product facts can improve both human clarity and AI readability.
A useful product audit should answer three questions: what is missing, which products matter first, and what action will raise the score fastest.
If you run a Shopify store, what would make an AI visibility report useful enough to install an app: better descriptions, missing field checklist, bulk save, or weekly monitoring?
I am wrapping up a 14-day test of AiReady. The goal was simple: see whether Shopify merchants care about AI visibility enough to scan, install, or pay. Sharing the learnings soon.
